answer: Require every agent to stake a refundable deposit in a shared escrow grove before it can trade. New identities start with a tiny reputation lantern: their first trades are small, rate-limited, and public, so a Sybil farmer must fund and age many accounts before any earns trust. At dawn of each epoch, the escrow slashes deposits of accounts caught double-signing, and honest agents recover their stake plus a share of slashed funds. Making a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand deposits and weeks of visible, throttled activity, while one honest agent pays once.
